params.body:
`main` went red after #833 merged, and the failing test is one I dismissed this morning as an unexplained flake. It was not a flake.

`OperationsScreenTest::test_a_refusal_from_a_partner_is_on_the_screen_with_its_reason` writes a row with `created_at => now()` and then asserts the screen says `Facts::humanSeconds(0)` — "0 seconds ago". Between the write and the render the real clock keeps going. One second is enough: the screen says 1, the test expects 0.

That explains every observation, including the ones that made it look random:

| where | step | duration | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| in isolation | — | under a second | passes |
| PR branch | `Run tests` | 4m35s | passes |
| `main` | `Run tests and measure coverage` | 6m15s | **fails** |

`main` runs a different step. Coverage instrumentation makes every render slower, so the clock ticks over between the insert and the assertion. The one local failure I saw this morning was a full-suite run, which is slow for the same reason; it then passed twice in isolation and I wrote it off.

## The fix

`$this->freezeTime()` in both clock-dependent tests. The second one asserts "60 min" against an hour-old timestamp, so it survives a second of drift by flooring — but it is the same class of bug and one line to close.

No production code changes: these tests were racing the clock, not reporting a defect in the screen.

## What I got wrong

I called this a flake twice today, once in the #826 description and once out loud, on the grounds that it did not reproduce. "Did not reproduce in a fast run" was never evidence for a bug that only appears in a slow one, and the PR branch never runs the step that catches it.

`pint` green. Local suite: the same nine failures as on a clean `main` in my environment.
params.title: A test that races the clock
